prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1010; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Responding to a report of a two-vehicle collision at an intersection in Houston, Texas, I found that Driver 1 was making a left turn when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 reported back strain following the impact. The nature and force of the collision are consistent with that type of injury. A Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle, and both the responding officers and the statements taken at the scene confirm that Driver 1 was present in the vehicle at the time. No independent witnesses were located. Scene photographs show the damage and confirm several details provided by the drivers. The visible damage is largely consistent with the impact described. Nothing in the vehicle's condition or the records reviewed suggests earlier damage. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene, and the drivers exchanged information before leaving.
